messages:
Sam: Quick heads-up — OrionData wants a Dedicated dry-run for Q3. They propose 6k GPU hours/month and are asking to lock buffer at 5% for the trial. We usually require 20%. Any immediate red flags?
Anya: Region detail? if that 6k is across APAC+EU we need to think about cross-region replication and spare capacity for failover.
Miguel: 5% buffer is scary for tail latencies. KV-cache warmups + transformer cold-starts mean microbursts could push p99 way up. Also queue depth may cause backpressure and increased token cost.
Devin: We can run a quick Monte Carlo on their profile. If they give us hourly QPS distribution for the last 3 months I can simulate headroom for different buffer levels.
Sam: They sent a coarse hourly heatmap, peaks around local 11-13h, 28% of traffic in that window.
Devin: Perfect. I'll run sims for 5%, 10%, and 20% buffer and include p50/p95/p99 token latency and GPU-util tail-risk. Command I'll run:```bash
./tools/sim_commit_gap.py --hours 6000 --profile orion_heatmap.json --buffers 0.05,0.1,0.2 --out results/orion-dryrun.csv
```
Anya: Also note billing/contract side — finance needs to know whether we do a prorated commit if they escalate mid-quarter. @finance-bot any quick estimate on cost delta between 5% and 20% buffer for 6k hours?
finance-bot: Estimated delta: ~+12k USD/month if we require 20% vs 5% (back-of-envelope, depends on instance mix and preemption exposure). Reach out if you want a formal quote.
Miguel: Another operational point — if we accept 5% buffer for dry-run we should require automatic fallback rules: route overflow to shared pool with degraded QoS, and set a hard circuit-breaker at 30% overcommit. Otherwise we'll jeopardize other tenants.
Sam: Agreed. Proposal: allow a 30-day dry-run at 5% buffer with canary (10% of traffic) for first 7 days, automatic fallback to shared pool, plus an opt-in 10% buffer ramp if p99 > 200ms. Thoughts?
Devin: Sounds sensible. I'll prioritize the sim and include a scenario with network egress incidents (packet loss spikes) because cross-region failovers amplify latency. Expect results by EOD.
Anya: Customer SLA tolerance documented as p99 <= 200ms during peak and 99.9% uptime. That gives us a guardrail to trigger buffer ramp.
Miguel: One more: schedule a network test with @sre-bot to validate failover latencies EU<->US and APAC<->US before we sign anything. Shared pool fallback numbers must be observable.
sre-bot: Noted — I'll run synthetics on the failover paths and report 95/99 latency impact. ETA 24h.
Sam: I'll draft the amendment: 30-day dry-run, 5% starting buffer, canary 10% traffic first week, auto-fallback to shared pool, automated ramp to 10% if p99>200ms, and 30% hard circuit-breaker. Tagging @Devin for simulation output and @sre-bot for network metrics. :thumbsup:
